questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

A lot of social work is __hindered__ due to corrupt politicians.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 (Obstructed)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"hindered"** means to create difficulties for someone or something, resulting in delay or obstruction. (बाधा डालना)

 
 
• **Example:** The heavy rain hindered the progress of the construction work.
 
 
 
• **"Obstructed"** means to block or get in the way of something, preventing it from progressing or continuing. (रोकना)
 
 
• **Example:** The fallen tree obstructed the road, making it impassable for vehicles.
 
 
 
• Hence, the synonym of **'hindered'** is **'obstructed'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (Obstructed)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Collided** (टकराना): To come into violent contact while moving.

 
 
• **Example:** The two cars collided at the intersection, causing a massive traffic jam.
 
 
 
• **Helped** (मदद करना): To assist or support someone in achieving something.
 
 
• **Example:** She helped her friend in completing the project on time.
 
 
 
• **Abided** (पालन करना): To accept or act in accordance with a rule, decision, or recommendation.
 
 
• **Example:** The citizens abided by the new regulations imposed by the government.

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into positive degree.

The dog is the most faithful animal.

options.text: The dog is more useful than any other animal.
The dog is the faithful animal.
No other animal is as faithful as the dog.
The dog is the only faithful animal.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence "The dog is the most faithful animal" is in the **superlative degree**. It indicates that the dog possesses the quality of faithfulness to the highest degree among all animals.

 
 
• **Example:** Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world.
 
 
 
• To change a superlative sentence into the **positive degree**, we need to express the quality without comparison, or by comparing it equally with others, often using phrases like "as...as" or "so...as."
 
• Let's analyze the options:
 
 
• **1) The dog is more useful than any other animal.** This sentence is in the **comparative degree** ("more useful than") and changes the adjective from "faithful" to "useful," which is incorrect.
 
• **2) The dog is the faithful animal.** This sentence is in the **positive degree** but it doesn't convey the same level of faithfulness implied by the superlative. It simply states a fact without comparison.
 
• **3) No other animal is as faithful as the dog.** This sentence correctly converts the superlative into the positive degree. It uses the "as...as" structure to state that no other animal possesses the quality of faithfulness to the same extent as the dog, thereby implying the dog's supreme faithfulness without using the superlative form.
 
 
• **Example:** No other city is as beautiful as Paris. (Converting "Paris is the most beautiful city.")
 
 
 
• **4) The dog is the only faithful animal.** This sentence expresses an exclusive statement, which is a different meaning from the original superlative statement. While it suggests high faithfulness, it's not the standard conversion to the positive degree.
 
 
 
• Therefore, "No other animal is as faithful as the dog" is the most accurate transformation to the positive degree while retaining the original meaning of the dog's superior faithfulness.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Degrees of Comparison:**

 
 
• **Positive Degree:** Used to describe a quality without comparison (e.g., *faithful*, *big*, *happy*).
 
• **Comparative Degree:** Used to compare two things (e.g., *more faithful than*, *bigger than*, *happier than*).
 
• **Superlative Degree:** Used to compare three or more things, indicating the highest or lowest degree of a quality (e.g., *most faithful*, *biggest*, *happiest*).
 
 
 
• **Transforming Superlative to Positive:**
 
 
• **Rule:** When converting a superlative degree sentence (e.g., "X is the most ADJECTIVE Y") to a positive degree, start with "No other Y is as ADJECTIVE as X" or "No other Y is so ADJECTIVE as X."

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

My mother is 51 years old, / and my uncle is 48 years old. / So my mother is old than my uncle.

options.text: and my uncle is 48 years old.
So my mother is old than my uncle.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. So my mother is old than my uncle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the phrase **"So my mother is old than my uncle."**
 
• The correct comparative form of the adjective **'old'** is **'older'**, not **'old.'**
 
• Comparative adjectives are used to compare two entities, and the correct usage in this context is **'older than.'**

Correct sentence: *My mother is 51 years old, and my uncle is 48 years old. So my mother is **older than** my uncle.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Adjectives:**
 
 
• Comparative adjectives are formed by adding **'-er'** to the base adjective (e.g., old → older) or using **'more'** before the adjective (e.g., beautiful → more beautiful).
 
• They are followed by the word **'than'** to indicate the comparison.
 
• **Example:** She is taller than her brother.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Adjectives:**
 
 
• Superlative adjectives are formed by adding **'-est'** to the base adjective (e.g., old → oldest) or using **'most'** before the adjective (e.g., beautiful → most beautiful).
 
• They are used to compare more than two entities.
 
• **Example:** She is the tallest in the class.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My sister is allergic with peanuts, so be cautious when preparing her meal.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. allergic with peanuts .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"allergic with peanuts"** is incorrect. The correct preposition to use with the word "allergic" is **"to"**, not "with."
 
• The word "allergic" is commonly followed by "to" when referring to the substance causing the allergic reaction.
 
• Thus, the correct phrase is: **"allergic to peanuts"**.

Correct sentence: *My sister is allergic to peanuts, so be cautious when preparing her meal.*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common Errors with Prepositions:**

 
 
• **Incorrect:** She is allergic with pollen.
 
• **Correct:** She is allergic to pollen.
 
• **Explanation:** The word "allergic" requires the preposition "to" to correctly describe the relationship between the person and the allergen.
 
 
 
• **Usage Tips:**
 
 
• When describing allergies, always use "to" with the word "allergic."
 
• Example: "He is allergic to shellfish."
 
 
</ul

questions.question:

• **Example:** The teacher had to draw on her experience to handle the challenging situation in the classroom.
 
 
 
• **"Imagination"** refers to the ability of the mind to be creative or resourceful in thinking about things that are not real or present. (कल्पना शक्ति)
 
 
• **Example:** The artist's imagination helped her create a masterpiece that captured the beauty of nature.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the poet "drew on his fancy," which implies he used his imagination to compose his sonnets. (यहां कवि ने अपनी कल्पना शक्ति का उपयोग किया।)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'opacity' in the given sentence.

The diminishing and deteriorating visibility in winter leads to the revival of accident cases on the highway.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 (Visibility)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"opacity"** means the state of being opaque or not transparent; it refers to a lack of clarity or transparency. (अस्पष्टता)

 
 
• **Example:** The opacity of the frosted glass ensures privacy in the office.
 
 
 
• **"Visibility"** is the antonym of "opacity." It refers to the state of being able to see or be seen clearly; it indicates clarity or transparency. (दृश्यता)
 
 
• **Example:** The visibility on the highway improved after the fog lifted.
 
 
 
• Hence, the antonym of **"opacity"** is **"visibility."**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (Visibility)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Diminishing** (घटता हुआ): Becoming smaller or less significant.

 
 
• **Example:** The diminishing light of the sunset created a serene atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Revival** (पुनर्जीवन): The act of bringing something back to life or into use.
 
 
• **Example:** The revival of traditional crafts has boosted the local economy.
 
 
 
• **Deteriorating** (बिगड़ता हुआ): Becoming progressively worse.
 
 
• **Example:** The deteriorating condition of the roads makes travel dangerous.

questions.question:

Shyam approached an leading psychologist for his treatment of anxiety and depression.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. an leading psychologist contains an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **“an”** is incorrectly used before the adjective “leading.”
 
• The article **“an”** is used before words that start with a vowel sound, whereas **“leading”** begins with a consonant sound.
 
• The correct article to use in this case is **“a.”**

Correct sentence: *Shyam approached **a leading psychologist** for his treatment of anxiety and depression.*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **An:** Used before words starting with vowel sounds (e.g., an apple, an hour).
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Using “an” before words with consonant sounds.
 
• Using “a” before words with vowel sounds.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Our team lost the game / only because of / a mistake / with one of our players.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. with one of our players .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "with one of our players" contains a grammatical error because "with" is not the correct preposition in this context.
 
• The correct preposition should be "by," as the mistake was committed by one of the players.
 
• Prepositions are crucial in conveying the right relationship between elements in a sentence.

Correct sentence: *Our team lost the game only because of a mistake **by** one of our players.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Prepositions:**

 
 
• Prepositions are words that link nouns, pronouns, or phrases to other words within a sentence.
 
• They often describe relationships of location, direction, cause, or possession.
 
• For example, "by" indicates the agent performing an action, while "with" often indicates accompaniment or an instrument used.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**

 
 
• Using incorrect prepositions leads to confusion or incorrect meanings.
 
• Always ensure the preposition aligns with the intended meaning of the sentence.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Ramgopal __is having__ a very big house in Mumbai.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. has .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence in question is: *"Ramgopal is having a very big house in Mumbai."*
 
• The verb **"is having"** is incorrect in this context because the verb "have" (when referring to possession) is a stative verb. Stative verbs are not usually used in the continuous form.
 
• Instead, the simple present tense **"has"** should be used to indicate possession.

Correct sentence: *Ramgopal **has** a very big house in Mumbai.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stative Verbs:**

 
 
• Stative verbs describe states, emotions, possession, senses, or opinions rather than actions.
 
• Examples: have, know, believe, love, hate, etc.
 
• These verbs are generally not used in continuous forms.
 
• For example:
 
 
• Correct: I **have** a car.
 
• Incorrect: I **am having** a car.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Dynamic Verbs:**
 
 
• Dynamic verbs describe actions or processes that can be continuous.
 
• For example:
 
 
• Correct: She **is running** in the park.
 
• Correct: I **am eating** dinner.

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

They had a __least__ celebration on her birthday.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. little .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the phrase **"a least celebration"**, which is grammatically incorrect. The correct expression should refer to a small or minimal celebration.
 
• The word **"little"** is appropriate to describe the extent or intensity of the celebration in this context.
 
• Other options, such as **"less," "most less,"** and **"lesser,"** do not fit grammatically or contextually in this sentence.

Correct sentence: *They had a little celebration on her birthday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
